```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(psych)
library(knitr)

# ---- Load cleaned data (produced by 02_clean_B.R) ----
if (!file.exists("Data_B_clean.rds"))
  stop("Run 02_clean_B.R first to produce Data_B_clean.rds")
Data_B <- readRDS("Data_B_clean.rds")

# ---- Raw-state constants ----
n_raw      <- 199
n_raw_cols <- 40

# ---- Helper functions ----
fmt <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) return("—")
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
}

num_table <- function(df, vars, labels) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(vars), function(v) {
    x <- df[[v]]
    data.frame(
      Variable = labels[[v]],
      n        = sum(!is.na(x)),
      Missing  = sum(is.na(x)),
      Mean     = fmt(mean(x,   na.rm = TRUE)),
      SD       = fmt(sd(x,     na.rm = TRUE)),
      Median   = fmt(median(x, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      Min      = fmt(min(x,    na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      Max      = fmt(max(x,    na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

# ---- Defensive check: recoded columns exist ----
required <- c("marital_clean","education_clean","disease_clean","regimen_clean",
              "condom_clean","alcohol_clean","smoking_clean","transport_clean",
              "sport_clean","art_start_year")
missing_cols <- setdiff(required, names(Data_B))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0)
  stop("Missing recoded columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       ". Re-run 02_clean_B.R.")
```

## Data cleaning and preparation
The raw dataset contained `r n_raw` records and `r n_raw_cols` variables, all initially stored as character strings. The following changes were made before analysis. The full cleaning code is in `Data_B_clean.R`; this section describes *what* was done.

## 1.Column name normalisation
Original Excel headers contained spaces and inconsistent capitalisation (e.g. `No. of sexual partners`, `no of H/H members`). These were standardised to snake_case using `janitor::clean_names()`.


## 2.Missing-value codes harmonised
The string codes `"no record"`, `"n/a"`, `"n.a"`, `"m/a"`, `"np"`, `"no mention"`, and `"NA"` were converted to `NA`. Character fields were trimmed and lowercased.

## 3.Numeric variables extracted from text
Several numeric variables were stored as descriptive text and were parsed:

age — plain numeric years.

no_of_h_h_members — e.g. "4 H/H members".

no_of_sexual_partners — spelled-out numbers converted; "no sexual partner" coded as 0.

children_ever_born — "nil"/"none" → 0.

viral_load_level_on_initiation / viral_load_on_reincoportation — parsed to numeric (copies/mL).

cd4_vount_level / cd4_on_reincorporation — parsed to numeric (cells/µL).

## 4.Date parsing and year of ART initiation
Values in length_of_time_on_art were ART start dates written as text (e.g. "since 4 march 21"), not durations. These were parsed to dates after correcting month-name typos.

Because the data-collection date was not recorded in the dataset, time on ART could not be computed. Year of ART initiation is reported instead.

## 5.Excel date serials in duration fields
Records in period_on_tb_treatment and length_of_time_on_art that contained 5-digit values (44,000–45,000) consistent with Excel date serials were set to missing. Records marked "never been on isoniazid" were coded as 0 months of TB treatment.

## 6.Categorical harmonisation
Typos and casing variants were collapsed:

Yes/no fields — "yrs" → yes; "no." → no.

Educational level — "sprimary schooling" → primary.

Disease status — "HV" → HIV; "both HIV TB" → HIV & TB.

Regimen — "Both HIV & TB treatment" → ART & TB.

Condom use — "no, to condom use" → no.

Transport — 
"walkkng"
 → walking.

Marital status — "maiied" → married.

## 7.Variables excluded
Two variables were dropped: residential_area (all records were urban) and type_of_religion (all records were Christianity). Neither had any variance.

## 8.Missing data
Missing values were not imputed. Two kinds of missingness are distinguished in the tables:

Data missingness — information that should have been recorded but was not.

Structural missingness — information that does not exist for certain patients (e.g., LTFU period applies only to patients who were ever LTFU and returned).

## Results

## Numeric variables

```{r}
num_vars <- list(
  age_num             = "Age (years)",
  hh_members_num      = "Household members (n)",
  sexual_partners_num = "Sexual partners (n)",
  children_num        = "Children ever born (n)",
  time_on_tb_tx_num   = "TB treatment duration (months)",
  ltfu_period_num     = "LTFU period (months)",
  vl_initiation_num   = "Viral load at ART initiation (copies/mL)",
  cd4_initiation_num  = "CD4 at ART initiation (cells/µL)",
  vl_reincorp_num     = "Viral load at re-incorporation (copies/mL)",
  cd4_reincorp_num    = "CD4 at re-incorporation (cells/µL)"
)

kable(num_table(Data_B, num_vars, num_vars),
      caption = "Table 1. Summary of numeric variables.",
      align = c("l","r","r","r","r","r","r","r"))
```

## Year of ART initiation

```{r}
yr <- Data_B %>%
  filter(!is.na(art_start_year)) %>%
  count(art_start_year, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(`%` = sprintf("%.1f%%", n / sum(n) * 100)) %>%
  rename(Year = art_start_year)

kable(yr,
      caption = paste0("Table 2. Year of ART initiation (n = ",
                       sum(yr$n), ")."),
      align = c("l","r","r"))
```

## Categorical variables

```{r cat-tables, results='asis'}
cat_vars <- c(
  gender                        = "Gender",
  marital_clean                 = "Marital status",
  education_clean               = "Educational level",
  employment_status             = "Employment status",
  disease_clean                 = "Disease status",
  regimen_clean                 = "Regimen type",
  condom_clean                  = "Condom use",
  alcohol_clean                 = "Alcohol consumption",
  smoking_clean                 = "Smoking habit",
  transport_clean               = "Mode of transport to health facility",
  sport_clean                   = "Participation in sport",
  distance_from_health_facility = "Distance from health facility"
)

for (v in names(cat_vars)) {
  x <- Data_B[[v]]
  t <- table(x, useNA = "ifany")
  df <- data.frame(
    Category = names(t),
    n        = as.integer(t),
    `%`      = sprintf("%.1f%%", as.integer(t) / sum(t) * 100),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("\n\n**", cat_vars[[v]], "**\n\n", sep = "")
  # The fix is right here: use cat() instead of print()
  cat(kable(df, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l","r","r")), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

## Notes on interpretation
Viral load units. Viral load is reported in copies/mL as recorded in the source data.

Structural missingness. LTFU period and re-incorporation VL/CD4 have high missingness because these variables are only applicable to the subset of patients who were LTFU and returned to care. These rates should not be interpreted as data-quality failures.

Time on ART could not be computed because the data-collection date was not recorded; year of ART initiation is reported instead (Table 2).

LTFU Definition: During cleaning, patients recorded as "died on 22 May 23" were excluded from the binary LTFU outcome (NA) to avoid competing-risk bias, meaning they are not counted as events or non-events.

## Logistic Regression: Predictors of LTFU

To identify independent predictors of LTFU, a multivariable logistic regression model was fitted.

```{r}
library(broom)
library(pROC)
library(ResourceSelection)

# 1. Recreate the outcome variable
Data_B <- Data_B %>%
  mutate(ltfu = case_when(
    str_detect(ever_ltfu, "^y") ~ 1,
    str_detect(ever_ltfu, "^n|never") ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  ))

# 2. Fit the model (using the significant predictors from univariable screening)
form_clean <- ltfu ~ gender + education_clean + smoking_clean + alcohol_clean + 
                      condom_clean + hh_members_num + disease_clean
                      
multi_clean <- glm(form_clean, data = Data_B, family = binomial)

# 3. Print the table (with publication-ready row names)
tidy(multi_clean, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    Predictor = case_when(
      term == "gendermale" ~ "Male gender",
      term == "education_cleansecondary" ~ "Education: Secondary",
      term == "education_cleantertiary" ~ "Education: Tertiary",
      term == "smoking_cleanyes" ~ "Smoking",
      term == "alcohol_cleanyes" ~ "Alcohol consumption",
      term == "condom_cleanno" ~ "Condom use: No",
      term == "condom_cleanyes" ~ "Condom use: Yes",
      term == "hh_members_num" ~ "Household members",
      term == "disease_cleanHIV & TB" ~ "Disease: HIV & TB",
      term == "disease_cleanTB" ~ "Disease: TB",
      TRUE ~ term
    ),
    OR = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
    CI = sprintf("%.2f - %.2f", conf.low, conf.high),
    p  = ifelse(p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value))
  ) %>%
  select(Predictor, OR, CI, p) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Adjusted Odds Ratios for Loss to Follow-Up (Data B)")

# 4. Calculate metrics for the text below
auc_val <- round(as.numeric(pROC::auc(pROC::roc(multi_clean$y, multi_clean$fitted.values, quiet = TRUE))), 3)
hl_p    <- round(ResourceSelection::hoslem.test(multi_clean$y, multi_clean$fitted.values, g = 10)$p.value, 3)
```

## Interpretation:
In the multivariable model, educational level was the primary independent predictor of LTFU. Compared to the reference group, patients with secondary education (Adjusted OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.15–0.97) and tertiary education (Adjusted OR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.01–0.62) had significantly lower odds of being lost to follow-up. Although variables such as gender, condom use, and alcohol consumption were significant in univariable analysis, they did not remain significant after adjusting for education.

**Model fit:** The model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC = `r auc_val`) and good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p = `r hl_p`).
